$comment: WriteMind built-in checker rules, shared by the Chrome extension (TypeScript) and the Windows app (C#). Patterns must stay compatible with both JavaScript and .NET regex. Offsets are UTF-16. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (Built-in checker).

confusionHelp.then: “Then” is about time or order (“and then we left”).
confusionHelp.there: “There” is a place, or starts a sentence like “there is”.
confusionHelp.form: “Form” is a document or a shape.
confusionHelp.from: “From” shows where something starts or comes from.
confusionHelp.of: “Of” shows belonging or a part (“a cup of tea”).
confusionHelp.off: “Off” is the opposite of on (“turn off the light”).
confusionHelp.lose: “Lose” is a verb: to fail to keep or win.
confusionHelp.loss: “Loss” is a noun: the act of losing.
confusionHelp.affect: “Affect” is usually a verb: to influence.
confusionHelp.effect: “Effect” is usually a noun: a result.
confusionHelp.accept: “Accept” means to receive or agree to.
confusionHelp.where: “Where” asks about or refers to a place.
confusionHelp.to: “To” shows direction or comes before a verb (“to go”).
confusionHelp.too: “Too” means also, or more than enough.
confusionHelp.know: “Know” means to be aware of something.
confusionHelp.new: “New” means recently made or not old.
confusionHelp.by: “By” means next to, or done by someone.
confusionHelp.write: “Write” means to put words on paper or a screen.
confusionHelp.right: “Right” means correct, or the opposite of left.
confusionHelp.hear: “Hear” means to listen with your ears.
confusionHelp.break: “Break” means to damage, or a pause.
confusionHelp.past: “Past” means earlier times, or beyond (“walked past”).
confusionHelp.thought: “Thought” is the past of “think”, or an idea.
confusionHelp.through: “Through” means from one side to the other.
confusionHelp.lead: “Lead” is the present tense (or a metal).
confusionHelp.wear: “Wear” is what you do with clothes.
confusionHelp.they: “They” refers to people or things (“they are”).
confusionHelp.council: “Council” is a group of people who decide things.
confusionHelp.does: “Does” is a form of “do” (“does he know?”).

rules.title: Spelling mistake
rules.message: “A lot” is written as two words.

rules.title: Commonly confused words
rules.message: Use “they're” (they are) when it means “they are …”.

rules.title: Wrong verb form
rules.message: After “did not / does not / do not”, use the base form “{=}”.

rules.title: Subject-verb agreement
rules.message: The subject is plural, so use “{=}”.

rules.title: Wrong verb form
rules.message: “{2}” needs “have”, or use the simple past “{=}”.

rules.title: Wrong verb form
rules.message: After “look forward to”, use the -ing form: “{=}”.

rules.title: Fewer vs. less
rules.message: Use “fewer” with things you can count.

rules.title: Pronoun case
rules.message: Use “I” as the subject of the sentence.

rules.title: Commonly confused words
rules.message: Use “to” before a noun (“too” means “also” or “excessively”).

rules.title: Capitalization
rules.message: Start the sentence with a capital letter.

rules.title: Spacing
rules.message: Add a space after the period.

rules.title: Extra space
rules.message: Use a single space between words.

rules.title: Repeated punctuation
rules.message: Repeated punctuation marks can read as unprofessional. Use a single mark.

rules.title: Contraction in formal writing
rules.message: Formal writing usually avoids contractions. Consider “{=}”.

rules.title: Informal language
rules.message: “{0}” is informal. Consider “{=}” for a more polished tone.

rules.title: Uncountable noun
rules.message: “{=}” is uncountable, so it has no plural form.

rules.title: Unnecessary word
rules.message: “{0}” repeats itself — the extra word isn't needed.

rules.title: Missing preposition
rules.message: We explain something to someone: “{1} to {2}”.

rules.title: Unnecessary preposition
rules.message: “Reach” takes no “to” before a place: “{1} the office”.

rules.title: Since or for
rules.message: Use “for” with a length of time (“for two years”) and “since” with a starting point (“since 2020”).

rules.title: Can / be able to
rules.message: Use “{1}” or “be able to”, not both.

rules.title: Introducing yourself
rules.message: To introduce yourself, say “I am …” or “My name is …”.

rules.title: One of + plural
rules.message: After “one of the/my …”, use the plural: “{=}”.

rules.title: Cannot
rules.message: “Cannot” is usually written as one word.

rules.title: Missing comma
rules.message: Put a comma after “{1}” at the start of a sentence.
rules.pattern: (?:^|(?<=[.!?]\s+)|(?<=\n))(However|Therefore|Moreover|Furthermore|In addition|In conclusion|For example|For instance|Firstly|Secondly|Thirdly|Finally|Additionally|Consequently|Nevertheless|Nonetheless|In fact|On the other hand|In my opinion|To sum up|In summary|In short|Unfortunately|Fortunately|Meanwhile|Otherwise|Lastly|Personally|Honestly|Hopefully|Surprisingly|Interestingly)(?=\s+(?!(?:for|much|many|long|hard|far|often|big|small|great|good|bad|little|few|soon|well|sure|close|likely|strange|odd)\b)[A-Za-z])

rules.title: Wordiness
rules.message: “The reason is because” repeats itself; use “the reason is that”.

rules.title: Idiom
rules.message: The idiom is “for all intents and purposes”.

rules.title: Clearer wording
rules.message: In international English, just say “your name”.

rules.title: Clearer wording
rules.message: “Do the needful” is unclear outside South Asia; say what you need.

rules.title: Clearer wording
rules.message: In international English, say “out of town”.

rules.title: Clearer wording
rules.message: “Revert” means to go back to an earlier state; to answer, use “reply”.

rules.title: Word choice
rules.message: Did you mean “from”? “Form” is a document or a shape.

rules.title: Word choice
rules.message: Use “there” here: “there is”, “there was”. “Their” means belonging to them.

rules.title: Word choice
rules.message: Did you mean “know”? “Now” means at this moment.

rules.title: Word choice
rules.message: Did you mean “from”? “Form” is a document or a shape.
